records.title: Smart India Hackathon
records.org: Ministry of Education Innovation Cell and AICTE
records.summary: A national team hackathon where college students solve problem statements from government and industry. Selected teams build their solution for the grand finale and compete for awards.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash awards for winning teams at the grand finale.

location.place: Online rounds, in-person grand finale in India

apply.what_you_need: Nomination by your college SPOC after an internal hackathon, in a team of six with at least one woman
apply.how_they_select: Internal college hackathon first, then nomination by the college SPOC

records.typical_window: Held every year; the 2026 registration closed on 30 September.
records.notes: Students cannot register directly. A college SPOC nominates teams selected through the internal hackathon. Teams have six members from the same college and must include at least one female member.

records.title: RevenueCat Shipaton
records.summary: A global mobile app hackathon where entrants build and ship a new app using RevenueCat. Eligible projects compete for cash prizes across product and themed categories.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prizes across product and themed categories for shipped apps.

apply.what_you_need: A new app shipped to an app store using RevenueCat during the contest
apply.how_they_select: Judges score eligible apps against the published product and category criteria.

records.typical_window: Held every year since 2024; the 2026 edition closed on 30 September.
records.notes: The main competition is for people who have reached the age of majority where they live. Entrants aged 13 or older may enter only the Next Gen Award with parental or guardian consent. Residents of sanctioned or locally prohibited territories are excluded.

records.title: Microsoft Imagine Cup
records.summary: A global startup competition for student founders building with Microsoft technology. Teams receive competition exposure, coaching opportunities and a chance to compete for prizes.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prizes, coaching and exposure for student startup teams.

apply.what_you_need: A team where every member is an enrolled student
apply.how_they_select: Microsoft and qualified judging panels score each round against the published criteria.

records.typical_window: The season usually opens around September and MVP submissions close in early January
records.notes: Entrants must be at least 18 as of 30 September 2025. Every team member must have been enrolled at an accredited degree-granting institution during the stated competition period. Sanctioned countries and regions listed in the rules are excluded.

records.title: Myntra HackerRamp WeForShe
records.summary: A women-only fashion technology hackathon for undergraduate engineering students. Teams receive mentoring, compete for prizes and may earn pre-placement interview opportunities.

benefit.what_you_get: Prizes, mentoring and possible pre-placement interviews for women engineering students.

apply.what_you_need: A team of two or three women undergraduate engineering students

records.typical_window: Registration has recently closed in late August or early September
records.notes: The latest official registration page found is the 2025 cycle. It lists undergraduate engineering students, female gender and teams of two to three, but does not name graduation years.

records.title: Tata Imagination Challenge
records.summary: An individual idea competition for full-time undergraduate and postgraduate students in India. Participants develop and pitch an idea for prizes and opportunities to interact with Tata leaders.

benefit.what_you_get: Prizes for the best ideas and chances to meet Tata leaders.

apply.what_you_need: An individual idea, followed by a two-minute pitch video and three short answers if shortlisted.
apply.how_they_select: Quiz and reasoning rounds lead to an idea pitch, panel defence and jury finale.

records.typical_window: Registration usually opens in August and closes in September
records.notes: Applicants must be full-time college students in a regular undergraduate or postgraduate course in India. The official page does not restrict the academic stream.

records.title: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow India
records.summary: An India innovation competition for people aged 14 to 22 who propose technology solutions to social problems. Shortlisted teams receive prototype funding and winners receive grants.

benefit.what_you_get: Prototype funding for shortlisted teams and grants for the four winning teams.
benefit.amount_text: A total grant of INR 2 Crore

location.place: Online application, later stages in Bengaluru and Delhi NCR

apply.what_you_need: An original science or technology concept from an individual or a team of up to three.
apply.how_they_select: Experts screen ideas, then evaluate video pitches, prototypes and jury presentations across four elimination stages.

records.typical_window: The 2026 application cycle closed on 30 June, before training began in July.
records.notes: Applicants must be Indian nationals aged 14 to 22. The official eligibility section lists no student, marks, backlog, gap, branch, graduation-year or work-experience requirement.

records.title: Anveshan Fellowship Programme
records.summary: A fellowship challenge for full-time bachelor’s and master’s students at Indian institutions. Teams design and build a complete engineering system with Analog Devices mentors.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prizes for the top three teams, plus hardware and mentorship for shortlisted teams.

location.place: Remote development, presentations at Analog Devices India

apply.what_you_need: A team of three to five students, a faculty adviser and a two to three page project proposal.
apply.how_they_select: Analog Devices shortlists proposals, reviews implementation rounds and chooses winners through an internal jury.

records.typical_window: Registration began 15 June and proposals closed 15 July for the 2026 cycle.
records.notes: Applicants may be any nationality but must remain full-time students at an accredited Indian institution through the March 2027 finals. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: James Dyson Award India
records.summary: A design engineering competition for current university students and recent graduates. Entrants submit an invention that solves a real-world problem for national and global cash awards.

benefit.what_you_get: A cash prize for the India national winner, with larger global prizes available.

location.place: India national round with global judging

apply.what_you_need: A design or engineering invention and an online entry explaining the problem and solution.
apply.how_they_select: National design and engineering panels shortlist entries before Dyson engineers and James Dyson choose global winners.

records.typical_window: Entries opened 11 March and closed at midnight on 15 July in 2026.
records.notes: Current students and recent graduates of design and engineering subjects may apply. The official page lists no marks, backlog, gap, graduation-year, citizenship or work-experience cutoff.

records.title: TCS CodeVita
records.summary: A recurring global programming competition for science and engineering students. Coders advance through ranked rounds to a finale with cash prizes for the top three.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prize money for the top three coders.

location.place: Online rounds, Season 14 grand finale in India

apply.what_you_need: Individual registration and the ability to code in C, C++, Java or Python.
apply.how_they_select: Coders solve timed programming problems, with top-ranked participants advancing through successive rounds.

records.typical_window: Season 14 registration was open on the official page in September 2026, but no closing date was printed.
records.notes: Eligibility covers graduation or post-graduation students in any science or engineering stream at recognized institutes worldwide.

records.title: Meta Hacker Cup
records.summary: Meta’s annual worldwide programming competition. Individuals solve algorithmic problems in online rounds and top competitors advance to a cash-prize final.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prizes for the top 25 competitors in the final round.

apply.what_you_need: Individual registration and algorithmic solutions submitted during the online rounds.
apply.how_they_select: Scores and tie-break rules rank each round, with the top 25 from Round 3 advancing to the final.

records.typical_window: Registration for the 2025 season opened on 3 October and online rounds ran from October through December.
records.notes: The official landing page describes the competition as open to participants around the world and does not require student status.

records.title: Amazon ML Challenge
records.summary: A recurring machine learning competition for engineering students at Indian campuses. Teams build models on an Amazon dataset and finalists present to Amazon scientists.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prizes for the top three teams, plus pre-placement interviews for the top 50.

apply.what_you_need: A team of two to four eligible students and a valid AWS Builder Center Profile ID alias.
apply.how_they_select: A 72-hour machine learning leaderboard and solution document determine the top ten teams for the virtual grand finale.

records.typical_window: The 2026 registration stage ran during September.
records.notes: Applicants must pursue a listed full-time engineering degree at an engineering campus in India and graduate in 2027 or 2028.

records.title: ETHGlobal Hackathons
records.summary: A recurring series of online and in-person web3 hackathons. Builders create open-source projects, receive technical mentorship and compete for sponsor prizes.

benefit.what_you_get: Sponsor cash prizes, including multiple tracks at each event.
benefit.amount_text: $15,000 (one sponsor pool at ETHOnline 2026; other tracks pay separately)

location.place: ETHOnline is global and online; other editions are in person

apply.what_you_need: An event application, then a project repository and supporting submission materials.
apply.how_they_select: Judges assess technicality, originality, practicality, usability and overall impact.

records.typical_window: ETHGlobal runs multiple events each year; ETHOnline 2026 accepted applications before its 4 September start.
records.notes: The amount shown is one printed ETHOnline 2026 sponsor pool, The Graph at $15,000. Other sponsor tracks carry separate printed amounts.

records.title: Bajaj Finserv HackRx
records.summary: Bajaj Finserv Health’s annual flagship hackathon for engineering students across India. Teams solve a sponsored technology problem and finalists compete for cash prizes.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prizes and pre-placement interview opportunities.

apply.what_you_need: A team of two to five undergraduate or postgraduate engineering students.
apply.how_they_select: Teams build against the published problem and selected finalists present their solution to the jury.

records.typical_window: Registration for HackRx 6.0 closed on 8 August 2025.
records.notes: The official registration page identifies undergraduate, postgraduate and engineering students but does not name a graduation batch.

records.title: Hack This Fall
records.summary: A recurring builder hackathon with a worldwide virtual edition and optional build stations in India. Teams create projects, receive mentorship and compete for cash prizes.

benefit.what_you_get: Organizer and partner cash prizes across open and technology tracks.

location.place: Worldwide virtual event, build stations and demo day in India

apply.what_you_need: A hackathon application, followed by a project submission for participating teams.
apply.how_they_select: Top projects are invited to a Bengaluru demo day and compete for organizer and partner prizes.

records.typical_window: The 2025 milestone edition ran as a month-long virtual hackathon in November.
records.notes: The official page welcomes builders worldwide and explicitly says first-time hackers and seasoned builders are welcome.

records.title: Google Summer of Code
records.summary: A global program for students and beginner open source contributors to build a project with a mentoring organization. Accepted contributors receive mentorship and a stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: A stipend paid over the coding period, sized by project length and your country.

apply.what_you_need: A project proposal prepared for one of the accepted mentoring organizations.
apply.how_they_select: Mentoring organizations review and rank contributor proposals before Google allocates slots.

records.typical_window: Contributor proposals usually open in March and close near the end of March
records.notes: Applicants must be at least 18, be eligible to work in their country of residence, and be a student or a beginner to open source. Residents of embargoed countries and some prior participants are excluded.

records.title: LFX Mentorship
records.summary: A set of mentored open source projects offered by Linux Foundation communities. Mentees work with project mentors, and eligible projects may include a stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: A mentored project; paid terms starting on or after July 1, 2026 use a total stipend set by country.

apply.what_you_need: An LFX mentee profile and an application to a listed mentorship project.
apply.how_they_select: The project administrator reviews each application and contacts candidates with next steps.

records.typical_window: Project applications are commonly open for about four weeks before spring, summer, and fall terms
records.notes: Applicants must be at least 18 and legally able to participate where they live. Each project can add prerequisites and its own exact deadline, so check the selected project before applying.

records.title: MLH Fellowship
records.summary: A remote 12-week program where fellows build software and can contribute to open source with a cohort. Fellows receive structured experience and a stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: A stipend for the 12-week remote program.

apply.what_you_need: A resume or online profile, coding proficiency, and prior MLH event attendance.

records.typical_window: Batches run during the year, with deadlines announced for each term
records.notes: The Fall 2026 application requires applicants to be over 18, commit at least 20 hours per week, code proficiently in at least one language, communicate in English, and have attended an MLH Hackathon or Global Hack Week event. Residents of US-embargoed countries are excluded.

records.title: Outreachy
records.summary: A paid remote internship in open source for people who face underrepresentation, systemic bias, or discrimination in their local technology industry. Interns receive mentorship and a USD 7,000 stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: A USD 7,000 stipend for a paid remote internship with a mentor.

apply.what_you_need: An initial application with essays, followed by a recorded contribution and final application.
apply.how_they_select: Organizers review initial eligibility and essays, then project mentors select interns after contributions.

records.typical_window: For Indian university students, initial applications usually open in early February for the May to August cohort
records.notes: This is not women-only. Applicants from any underrepresented background may apply. Applicants must be at least 18 and available for 30 hours per week. Indian university students are treated as Northern Hemisphere students and may apply only to the May to August cohort; non-students may apply to either cohort. Prior Outreachy, Outreach Program for Women, and Google Summer of Code interns are ineligible.

records.title: Summer of Bitcoin
records.summary: A global online summer internship for university and high school students contributing to Bitcoin open source projects. Accepted students work with mentors and earn a Bitcoin stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: A stipend paid in Bitcoin for the 12-week internship.

apply.what_you_need: A coding or design portfolio, bootcamp challenge solutions, and a project proposal.
apply.how_they_select: Selection uses bootcamp solutions, proposal quality, and proactive project contributions.

records.typical_window: Applications usually run during the first half of February
records.notes: Applicants need programming or design skills and open source experience. The program expects full-time availability for the 12-week summer internship and regular contact with mentors.

records.title: FOSSEE Summer Fellowship
records.summary: A summer fellowship where students complete screening tasks and work with a FOSSEE team on free and open source software. Successful fellows receive an e-certificate and a published-work link, but the program does not provide an honorarium.

benefit.what_you_get: An e-certificate and a published-work link. The program does not pay an honorarium.

location.place: Online, confirm on the fellowship page

apply.what_you_need: Completed screening tasks for the project you pick
apply.how_they_select: Screening tasks, then selection by the FOSSEE team

records.typical_window: Registrations usually open in March and the fellowship starts in May
records.notes: The official fellowship page says it is open to students from any college, pursuing any degree, at any stage of undergraduate or postgraduate study, and that the only selection criterion is the successful completion of a useful project after the screening tasks. It prints no marks, backlog or gap cutoff. The 2026 fellowship is over and its results were published on 18 September 2026; the 2027 registration date is not announced yet, so watch the fellowship page around March.

records.title: Hacktoberfest
records.summary: A worldwide October celebration with in-person and online events focused in 2026 on open source AI. Participants can learn, build projects, and may receive event prizes or swag where offered.

benefit.what_you_get: Event prizes or swag where the event you attend offers them. No stipend.

location.place: Open worldwide, online and local events

apply.what_you_need: Registration for an online or local Fest and any materials required by that event.

records.typical_window: Hacktoberfest 2026 runs through October 2026 with 300+ in-person and online events; each event publishes its own date and registration link.
records.notes: Anyone aged 13 or older may participate, subject to US export controls and embargo restrictions. The official FAQ gives no single participant registration deadline because attendance is through individual events; check the selected event for its date.

records.title: Season of KDE
records.summary: A mentored KDE program for code and non-code projects that benefit the KDE ecosystem. Participants who complete their projects receive a certificate and merchandise.

benefit.what_you_get: A certificate and KDE merchandise on completing the project. No stipend.

apply.what_you_need: Contact with the KDE community, a potential mentor, and a project proposal.
apply.how_they_select: KDE mainly selects applicants who discussed their proposal and started engaging with the project.

records.typical_window: Applications generally run from December to mid January
records.notes: The program is open to everyone, not only enrolled students. KDE says rules can vary by season and recommends contacting the community and a potential mentor before applying.

records.title: Igalia Coding Experience
records.summary: A remote-friendly paid mentorship for people seeking their first professional open source experience. Participants complete 450 hours with an Igalia mentor.

benefit.what_you_get: Financial compensation for 450 hours completed over three or six months.

apply.what_you_need: An application for one of the listed technical areas and a workable three or six month schedule.

records.typical_window: Applications usually open in late February and close in early April.
records.notes: Formal students, self-taught learners, and career changers without tech work experience may apply. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Open Source Promotion Plan
records.org: Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences
records.summary: A rolling program where enrolled university students worldwide complete open source projects with mentors. Successful participants receive remuneration and a certificate.

benefit.what_you_get: Pre-tax remuneration after the project passes its completion assessment.

apply.what_you_need: Proof of enrollment, a passport for international students, and a project application.
apply.how_they_select: Mentors, communities, and the organizing committee review the project application and proposal.

records.notes: Applicants must be at least 18 and remain enrolled through project development. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: OpenSSF Mentorship Program
records.summary: A paid remote mentorship in open source software security. Mentees work with project maintainers during a published annual cycle.

benefit.what_you_get: A paid mentorship with a country-adjusted educational stipend.

location.place: Open worldwide, subject to LFX rules

apply.what_you_need: An LFX mentee profile and an application to an available OpenSSF project.
apply.how_they_select: Applications are reviewed during the published selection period before notifications are sent.

records.typical_window: The 2026 cycle accepted applications from late March to mid April.
records.notes: The program describes a path for mentees breaking into open source and security beginners. The official eligibility page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Open Mainframe Project Mentorship
records.summary: A remote summer mentorship for higher education students working on Linux, open source, and mainframe projects. Selected mentees receive a stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: A stipend and mentorship on an open mainframe project.

location.place: Open worldwide, subject to LFX rules

apply.what_you_need: An LFX mentee profile and an application to one listed mainframe mentorship.
apply.how_they_select: Applications are reviewed and accepted during the two weeks before the term starts.

records.typical_window: Summer applications are generally open for about four weeks from mid April.
records.notes: The program page places the summer mentorship under Higher Education Students. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: LF Decentralized Trust Mentorship
records.summary: A structured remote mentorship for aspiring decentralized technology developers, researchers, and contributors. Paid projects use country-adjusted stipends.

benefit.what_you_get: A country-adjusted stipend in two installments when the selected project is paid.

location.place: Participants collaborate from their preferred locations

apply.what_you_need: An LFX profile and an application to a paid LF Decentralized Trust project.
apply.how_they_select: Program staff review applications and interview candidates before notifying selected mentees.

records.typical_window: The 2026 paid-project application period ran from late March to mid May.
records.notes: Some listed projects are unpaid, so choose one explicitly labeled as paid. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: CNCF LFX Mentorship
records.summary: A remote three-month mentorship on cloud native open source projects. Mentors select candidates for project-specific work and paid terms use LFX stipends.

benefit.what_you_get: A total country-adjusted LFX stipend for the term, paid after midterm and final evaluations.

location.place: Open worldwide, subject to LFX rules

apply.what_you_need: An LFX mentee profile and the prerequisites requested by the chosen CNCF project.
apply.how_they_select: Project mentors select the best fit using technical qualifications and ability to work with others.

records.typical_window: CNCF runs multiple terms; the 2026 fall term accepted applications in early August.
records.notes: Each project sets its own prerequisites, and not every project is necessarily funded. Check that the selected listing is paid and review its requirements before applying.

records.title: Science Academies Summer Research Fellowship Programme
records.org: Indian Academy of Sciences, INSA and NASI
records.summary: A two-month research placement with a scientist associated with one of India’s three national science academies. Selected fellows receive round-trip train fare and a monthly fellowship for living expenses.

benefit.what_you_get: Round-trip train fare and a monthly fellowship for two months at the host institute.

location.place: India, at the host scientist’s institute

apply.what_you_need: Your application and the email address of a teacher who can provide a recommendation.
apply.how_they_select: The Academies assign selected candidates to a guide and send results around March or April.

records.typical_window: The 2027 call opened on 10 September 2026 and closes on 30 November 2026; the call is usually announced in September for the following summer.
records.notes: The 2027 instructions admit BE, BTech and BCA students in the second and third year only, and BTech plus MTech dual degree students in years two to four. For the 2027 summer (academic year 2026-27) that means the 2029 and 2028 BTech batches, the 2028 and 2027 BCA batches, and the 2030, 2029 and 2028 dual degree batches, so all four years are listed and your degree type decides which apply. The academic rule is a single figure: the average of marks in core subjects only, excluding languages, from Class 10 through every completed year of study must be 65 percent or above. The app cannot compute that combined average from your profile, so the marks rules are left unconfirmed here; work it out yourself before applying. Students who have held the Academies fellowship twice before and PhD students are not eligible, and you must be studying in India. The fellowship amount is not printed on the pages read.

records.title: France Excellence Charpak Summer Training Scholarship
records.summary: A scholarship for an Indian student doing a one or two-month internship or research project at a French laboratory. It provides a monthly stipend, a student visa fee waiver and a Campus France procedure fee waiver.

benefit.what_you_get: A monthly stipend for one or two months in a French lab, plus a visa fee waiver and a Campus France fee waiver.
benefit.amount_text: EUR 700 per month for up to 2 months

apply.what_you_need: An invitation from a French laboratory or institution
apply.how_they_select: Selection considers academic excellence and the consistency and quality of the statement of purpose.

records.typical_window: The call is announced before internships held between May and August; the 2026 session is closed and the page says to watch the website for updates.
records.notes: The official page says the 2026 call is closed and does not print its deadline or the next one. It states that there is no CGPA or percentage cutoff. You must be an Indian national residing in India, be enrolled in an Indian institution at bachelor or master level, be no more than 30 years old at the time of application, and hold an invitation letter from the French laboratory or institution where the one to two month internship will take place.

records.title: IIT Madras Summer Fellowship Programme
records.summary: A guided summer research internship with IIT Madras faculty. The Engineering Design department describes it for BTech students who have completed six semesters.

benefit.what_you_get: A guided research internship at IIT Madras. The stipend for the next cycle is not stated on the pages read.

records.typical_window: The portal normally opens in February for the summer fellowship.
records.notes: The Engineering Design and Applied Mechanics department pages describe the programme for BTech students who have completed their sixth semester; for the closed 2026 cycle that meant the 2027 batch. Neither page prints a marks, backlog or gap cutoff. The central registration portal shows Registration Closed for 2026 without an eligibility page or the next deadline, so check the portal when it reopens for department-specific conditions. The central portal's own eligibility page could not be read, so the absence of a marks cutoff is unconfirmed until it reopens.

records.title: IUSSTF-Viterbi Program
records.org: Indo-U.S. Science and Technology Forum and USC Viterbi School of Engineering
records.summary: An eight-week full-time summer research placement for Indian engineering students at the USC Viterbi School of Engineering. It provides a stipend, airfare and accommodation.

benefit.what_you_get: A stipend, airfare and accommodation for eight weeks at USC Viterbi.

records.typical_window: Applications for the 2026 summer cohort closed at the end of December 2025.
records.notes: The official page also gives equivalents of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale or 80 percent. The structured cutoff uses only the explicitly stated 8.5 GPA value. Eligible students are in the third year of a four-year bachelor’s, the third or fourth year of a five-year bachelor’s, or the first year of a master’s, with degree completion on or after May 2027.

records.title: Technion Summer Research Program in Science and Engineering
records.summary: A one-month laboratory research program in Israel for international undergraduate students. Technion covers research costs, health insurance, accommodation, mentorship and social activities, while students pay airfare, most meals and local transport.

benefit.what_you_get: Research costs, health insurance, accommodation and mentoring are covered. You pay airfare, most meals and local transport.

records.typical_window: Applications close in late February for the July programme; the page announces the 2027 programme for July 2027 and says registration will open soon.
records.notes: The requirements page asks for undergraduates who have completed at least two years of study and a grade point average of 80 percent, given as 3.0 on a 4.0 scale; that degree bar is recorded here and not as a CGPA. For the February 2026 deadline (academic year 2025-26) completing two years by July meant the 2028 batch or earlier, so the closed cycle covered the 2026, 2027 and 2028 batches. Some Technion faculties add their own requirements. The scholarship covers accommodation and programme activities; you pay airfare, most meals and local transport. This degree bar is stated as a percentage or on a 4-point scale, which the app cannot compare with your 10-point CGPA, so the marks rule stays unconfirmed here and you must check it yourself.

records.title: Flipkart GRiD
records.summary: An online engineering challenge with software development, AI engineering and data science tracks. Strong performers can be interviewed for summer or winter internships and full-time roles, and Flipkart covers travel and stay for national finalists.

benefit.what_you_get: Interviews for internships and full-time roles for strong performers, with travel and stay covered for national finalists.

location.place: Online rounds, in-person finale in India

apply.what_you_need: Individual registration with accurate participant information before the deadline.
apply.how_they_select: Online challenge rounds, then interviews for strong performers

records.typical_window: Registration opened in mid-June and closed in mid-July for the 2026 edition.
records.notes: The official registration page permits bachelor’s and master’s graduation years 2027 to 2030. It also permits PhD and dual or integrated degree graduation years through 2031, which this BTech-focused record does not model.

records.title: CERN Summer Student Programme
records.summary: A summer research placement in physics, engineering, computer science or mathematics at CERN in Geneva. Students receive a daily allowance and may receive travel support.

benefit.what_you_get: A daily subsistence allowance, health insurance and possible travel support for the stay in Geneva.

apply.what_you_need: A CV in English or French and a completed online application.
apply.how_they_select: CERN reviews applications and may invite candidates to an online interview with hiring managers.

records.typical_window: Applications are normally due by the end of January for the following summer.
records.notes: Applicants must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree, not a PhD, and have completed at least six semesters by the start of summer. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: EPFL Excellence in Engineering Programme
records.summary: An 8 to 12 week summer research internship in an EPFL engineering laboratory. It provides a monthly allowance and covers travel costs.

benefit.what_you_get: A monthly allowance for accommodation and living costs, plus covered economy travel.

apply.what_you_need: An application package including a statement of purpose that identifies preferred host laboratories.
apply.how_they_select: Host laboratories screen applications and may interview candidates before competitive selection.

records.typical_window: Host laboratories screen applications after the portal closes and communicate outcomes around mid-March.
records.notes: Applicants must remain enrolled for the internship and must have completed at least the second bachelor year when applying. The page asks applicants to be in the top 10 percent of their class but gives no numeric CGPA conversion. It lists no school marks, backlog or gap cutoff. This degree bar is stated as a percentage or on a 4-point scale, which the app cannot compare with your 10-point CGPA, so the marks rule stays unconfirmed here and you must check it yourself.

records.title: ETH Student Summer Research Fellowship
records.org: ETH Zurich Department of Computer Science
records.summary: A two-month summer research fellowship in computer science or a related field at ETH Zurich. It includes a stipend and covered travel and visa expenses.

benefit.what_you_get: A stipend for housing and living expenses, with travel and visa expenses also covered.

apply.what_you_need: A CV, an official academic transcript and one or two preferred research areas.
apply.how_they_select: Applications are evaluated from the submitted documents, and shortlisted candidates may be interviewed.

records.typical_window: The next application window opens at the beginning of November 2026; the previous cycle closed on 16 December.
records.notes: Applicants must complete two years of study before the programme and expect to graduate in the year after the fellowship or later. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: University of Tokyo Research Internship Program
records.org: University of Tokyo Graduate School of Science
records.summary: A summer research internship in a University of Tokyo science laboratory. Participants receive a regional allowance and free housing.

benefit.what_you_get: A one-time allowance for airfare and daily expenses, plus free housing for 43 nights.

apply.what_you_need: Proof of English proficiency unless exempt, plus the required online application materials.
apply.how_they_select: Priority is given to third-year applicants in four-year degrees, while prepared second-year students are encouraged.

records.typical_window: The programme publishes a cycle-specific application schedule for its summer research placement.
records.notes: Applicants must have completed one bachelor year and must return to at least one academic term after UTRIP. The 140,000 JPY allowance is the official Asia-region amount. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Max Planck Computer Science Internship
records.org: Max Planck Institutes for Computer Science
records.summary: A research internship at a participating Max Planck computer science institute in Germany. It covers a stipend, housing and round-trip travel.

benefit.what_you_get: A monthly stipend, covered housing and round-trip travel to the host institute.

location.place: Participating Max Planck institutes in Germany

apply.what_you_need: A CV, transcripts, at least one reference contact and an optional motivation letter.
apply.how_they_select: Research groups review applications, may conduct a phone interview and match selected interns with a faculty mentor.

records.typical_window: The call runs every year; the deadline printed for 2027 internships was 1 November 2026.
records.notes: Applicants need coursework equivalent to the first three years of a computer science bachelor program or prior relevant research experience. Graduates and industry applicants may also apply. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: TIFR Hyderabad Visiting Students Research Programme
records.org: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Hyderabad
records.summary: An eight-week summer research project at TIFR Hyderabad. Selected students receive a monthly stipend, travel reimbursement and shared accommodation.

benefit.what_you_get: A monthly stipend, travel reimbursement under TIFR rules and free shared accommodation.

apply.what_you_need: An online application for the annual Visiting Students Research Programme call.

records.typical_window: The eight-week programme runs from May to July, and the 2026 application deadline was 31 January.
records.notes: BTech and BE students must be in their pre-final or final year; for the closed 2026 cycle (academic year 2025-26) that meant the 2027 and 2026 batches. Previous participants cannot apply again. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: IIT Gandhinagar Summer Research Internship Program
records.summary: An at least eight-week summer research project with an IIT Gandhinagar faculty mentor. Most in-person interns receive a weekly stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: A weekly stipend after completing the internship, with the amount varying for faculty-funded projects.

apply.what_you_need: A separate online application for each project, explaining research interests and relevant preparation.
apply.how_they_select: Faculty assess research interests, fit with the project and relevant previous exposure or training.

records.typical_window: The 2026 summer call closed on 5 March, with results expected by the end of March.
records.notes: The FAQ encourages first, second and third year undergraduate students; for the closed 2026 cycle (academic year 2025-26) that meant the 2029, 2028 and 2027 batches. Hostel accommodation costs INR 175 per day, so housing is not covered. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: UTokyo Amgen Scholars Program
records.org: University of Tokyo and Amgen Foundation
records.summary: An eight-week summer research internship in bioscience, biotechnology and related engineering fields at the University of Tokyo. It provides accommodation, travel support and a stipend.

benefit.what_you_get: Provided accommodation, travel support and a stipend for food, leisure and local programme travel.

apply.what_you_need: A TAO account, personal statement, official transcripts, proof of English proficiency and two recommendation letters.
apply.how_they_select: Selection begins after the application period rather than using rolling admission.

records.typical_window: The 2026 application deadline was 1 February for the eight-week summer programme.
records.notes: Applicants must attend a university in the eligible Asia region, complete at least one undergraduate year, and return for at least one academic term afterward; for the closed 2026 cycle (academic year 2025-26) that meant the 2029, 2028 and 2027 batches. Projects include bioengineering and chemical and biomolecular engineering. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Mitacs Globalink Research Internship
records.summary: A 12-week research internship for eligible Indian engineering undergraduates at a Canadian university. The award contributes to travel, housing, enrollment fees, food and incidentals.

benefit.what_you_get: Funding toward return airfare, airport transport, housing, enrollment fees, food and incidentals.

apply.what_you_need: Applications must select three to ten projects across at least three Canadian provinces.
apply.how_they_select: Mitacs ranks applicants and matches successful students with Canadian research projects.

records.typical_window: Student applications are made around June, and matching runs from September to December for internships the following summer.
records.notes: Indian applicants must be at least 18, study full time at an eligible non-IIT institution, be in BE or BTech, have 70 percent cumulative grades, and have one to three semesters remaining in fall 2027. The 70 percent degree requirement is not converted to min_cgpa. Applicants must be fluent in the project language. The page lists no Class 10, Class 12, backlog or gap cutoff. This degree bar is stated as a percentage or on a 4-point scale, which the app cannot compare with your 10-point CGPA, so the marks rule stays unconfirmed here and you must check it yourself.

records.title: MEXT Undergraduate Scholarship
records.org: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, Japan
records.summary: A Japanese Government scholarship for an undergraduate degree in Japan. It covers tuition, provides a monthly allowance and includes travel support under the scholarship guidelines.

benefit.what_you_get: Tuition covered, a monthly allowance and travel support for an undergraduate degree in Japan.

apply.what_you_need: Application form, transcripts, graduation certificate and a school recommendation letter
apply.how_they_select: The Embassy screens documents, written examinations and interviews, then MEXT makes the final selection

records.typical_window: Applications usually close in May for study beginning the following April
records.notes: This is a new undergraduate degree, not postgraduate study for a BTech student. Applicants must generally have been born on or after 2 April 2002 and must meet the schooling conditions in the guidelines. Applicants awaiting their 2027 Grade 12 result need 80% in Grade 10 plus a school prediction above 80%; this conditional rule is not stored as a Grade 10 cutoff.

records.title: Chevening Scholarship
records.summary: A scholarship for a one-year taught master’s degree at a UK university. It funds study and connects scholars with the Chevening network.

benefit.what_you_get: A funded one-year taught masters at a UK university.

apply.what_you_need: At least 2,800 hours of work experience after your degree, over two years or more
apply.how_they_select: Eligible applications are assessed against published criteria before shortlisted candidates are interviewed

records.typical_window: Opens every August and closes in the autumn; the 2027-28 round closed on 6 October 2026.
records.notes: A current undergraduate cannot apply. You must have finished your undergraduate degree at least two years before the deadline and have at least 2,800 hours of work experience gained after it, over a minimum of two years. The two year figure is the official minimum; the hours are checked by Chevening, not by this app.

records.title: Fulbright-Nehru Master’s Fellowships
records.summary: A fellowship for selected master’s programmes in the United States for Indian professionals. It provides tuition and fee funding, living support, travel, visa support and health coverage for up to two years.

benefit.what_you_get: Tuition and fees, living support, travel, visa support and health coverage for up to two years.

apply.what_you_need: Three years of relevant full-time paid work experience by the deadline
apply.how_they_select: USIEF reviews eligible applications and interviews shortlisted candidates before final nomination

records.typical_window: Applications usually close in May for programmes beginning the following year
records.notes: The official page still shows the 2026-27 cycle with its 14 May 2025 deadline, and USIEF has not published a 2027-28 master’s call yet. You need Indian citizenship, a completed bachelor’s degree with at least 55 percent marks (a degree percentage, so it is not entered as a CGPA) and at least three years of full-time paid professional work experience relevant to the proposed field. The page prints no backlog or gap rule. This degree bar is stated as a percentage or on a 4-point scale, which the app cannot compare with your 10-point CGPA, so the marks rule stays unconfirmed here and you must check it yourself.

records.title: Rhodes Scholarship for India
records.summary: A scholarship for full-time postgraduate study at the University of Oxford. Five scholarships are available for the India constituency.

benefit.what_you_get: Full funding for postgraduate study at the University of Oxford.

apply.what_you_need: An academic transcript, personal statement, passport evidence and referee details
apply.how_they_select: The India selection committee reviews applications and interviews shortlisted candidates

records.typical_window: Applications usually close in July for study beginning the following year
records.notes: Final-year students may apply, but the undergraduate degree must be complete by July 2027. The India constituency also applies education and residency tests. Applicants normally must be aged 18 to 23 on 1 October 2026, with a separate route for applicants under 27 who completed their first degree on or after 1 October 2025. The chosen Oxford course must accept the applicant’s academic background and grade.

records.title: Inlaks Scholarship
records.summary: A scholarship for Indian graduates pursuing selected programmes abroad. It contributes up to USD 120,000 toward programme expenses.

benefit.what_you_get: A contribution of up to USD 120,000 toward programme expenses abroad.

apply.what_you_need: An admission offer from the chosen programme, an Indian passport and residence in India
apply.how_they_select: Independent reviewers assess applications before shortlisted candidates attend preliminary and final interviews

records.typical_window: Applications usually close at the end of March
records.notes: Final-year undergraduates awaiting results may apply. Applicants must hold an Indian passport, reside in India at application, be born on or after 1 January 1996 for the 2026 call, and already hold an admission offer. Degree cutoffs vary by subject: 65% or 6.8/10 for listed humanities-related fields, and 70% or 7.2/10 for listed science-related fields, which is where engineering and natural sciences fall. The stored 6.8 is the floor below which nobody qualifies; for a science or engineering programme the bar is 7.2. Engineering and natural sciences are considered only at Imperial College London, so check course eligibility before applying. Because the bar depends on your subject, the stored 6.8 is only the lowest floor; treat the marks rule as unconfirmed until you match your field against the official list.

records.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
records.summary: Joint master’s programmes delivered by groups of universities in Europe and beyond. The best-ranked applicants may receive scholarships covering participation costs with contributions toward travel, visa and living costs.

benefit.what_you_get: Scholarships covering participation costs with contributions toward travel, visa and living costs, for the best-ranked applicants.

apply.what_you_need: A bachelor degree or proof you will graduate before the masters programme starts
apply.how_they_select: Each consortium ranks eligible applicants and awards scholarships to the best-ranked candidates

records.typical_window: Most programmes accept applications between October and January
records.notes: Final-year bachelor’s students may apply but must graduate before the master’s programme begins. Each consortium sets its own exact deadline, entry requirements and available subjects, so check the chosen programme’s official website. Because each consortium sets its own academic entry requirements, no cutoff can be confirmed absent here; treat the rules as unconfirmed until you read the chosen programme's page.

records.title: KAUST Fellowship
records.org: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
records.summary: Funding provided to admitted graduate students at KAUST in Saudi Arabia. It supports students for the duration of their graduate study and includes tuition, living and medical benefits.

benefit.what_you_get: Tuition, living and medical benefits for the whole graduate programme at KAUST.

apply.what_you_need: Admission to a KAUST graduate programme
apply.how_they_select: Faculty review complete applications and recommend candidates for admission

records.typical_window: Two rounds a year. A round closing in late September is for spring entry and PhD applicants only; the round for fall entry (MS and PhD) opens in late September and closes in early January.
records.notes: Master’s applicants need a bachelor’s degree in a subject relevant to the programme. The minimum GPA is stated as 3.0 on a 4-point scale or equivalent, so it is not converted to min_cgpa. The stored deadline is Fall 2027 Round 2 (MS, MS/PhD and PhD), which the timeline page calls tentative. The 27 September 2026 round is Spring 2027 entry for PhD applicants only. Confirm the intake and programme before applying. This degree bar is stated as a percentage or on a 4-point scale, which the app cannot compare with your 10-point CGPA, so the marks rule stays unconfirmed here and you must check it yourself.

records.title: Stipendium Hungaricum
records.summary: A Hungarian Government scholarship for eligible bachelor’s, master’s and other study programmes in Hungary. It provides tuition-free study, a stipend, accommodation support and medical insurance under the call.

benefit.what_you_get: Tuition-free study, a stipend, accommodation support and medical insurance under the call.

apply.what_you_need: The online form, motivation letter, proof of language, school certificates and transcripts
apply.how_they_select: Applications pass a technical check, sending-partner nomination and host-institution evaluation

records.typical_window: Applications usually close in mid January
records.notes: India appears in the official list of eligible sending partners. Available study levels and fields depend on the sending partner, and applications may also need submission to the responsible Indian authority under its own requirements and deadline. Check the India partner page and the next call before applying. Because the host university and the Indian sending authority set their own academic requirements, the rules stay unconfirmed until you read both.

records.title: Reliance Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
records.summary: A merit-cum-means scholarship for first-year undergraduate students in India. Selected scholars receive up to INR 2 lakh over their degree and access to networking and support.

benefit.what_you_get: Up to INR 2 lakh over your degree, plus networking and support.
benefit.amount_text: Up to INR 2 lakh over the degree

apply.what_you_need: Household income of INR 15 lakh or less and first-year enrolment in a full-time degree
apply.how_they_select: Mandatory aptitude test, then selection on merit and means

records.typical_window: Offered to each new first-year batch; the 2026-27 round closed on 5 October.
records.notes: Household income must be INR 15 lakh or less, with preference for applicants below INR 2.5 lakh. Applicants must be in the first year of a regular full-time undergraduate degree in academic year 2026-27, and an aptitude test is mandatory.

records.title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
records.summary: A full-cost scholarship for eligible postgraduate degrees at the University of Cambridge, including tuition, living support and travel.

benefit.what_you_get: Cambridge fees, a maintenance allowance and economy travel at the start and end of the course.

apply.what_you_need: A Cambridge course application, the Gates Cambridge funding questions and references
apply.how_they_select: Academic departments nominate candidates before Trust shortlisting and interviews

records.typical_window: Closes every December or early January with the Cambridge course deadline; the 2027 round closed on 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 depending on the course.
records.notes: Applicants must be citizens of a country outside the United Kingdom and apply for an eligible Cambridge postgraduate course. The official page lists no school marks, 10-point CGPA, backlog, gap or work-experience cutoff. The stored deadline is the earlier international course funding deadline; some courses close on 6 January 2027.

records.title: Schwarzman Scholars
records.summary: A fully funded one-year master’s in global affairs at Tsinghua University in Beijing, with tuition, living, travel and personal support.

benefit.what_you_get: Tuition, fees, room, board, travel, insurance, study costs and a personal stipend.

apply.what_you_need: An online form, resume, transcript, essays, recommendation letters and English test where required
apply.how_they_select: The admissions team reviews written applications and invites shortlisted candidates to a panel interview

records.typical_window: The next global application is scheduled to run from April to September 2027.
records.notes: Applicants must be 18 to 28 on 1 August of the enrolment year and complete their undergraduate degree requirements before 1 August. The programme expects demonstrated leadership. The official page lists no school marks, 10-point CGPA, backlog, gap or full-time work-experience cutoff.

records.title: Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships
records.summary: A scholarship for a one-year taught master’s in the United Kingdom for applicants from eligible Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford it.

benefit.what_you_get: Full tuition, return airfare, visa costs and a monthly living allowance.
benefit.amount_text: £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month in London

apply.what_you_need: A CSC application, passport or national ID, full transcripts and references
apply.how_they_select: A national nominator selects candidates before the CSC assesses academic merit and development impact

records.typical_window: Runs every year and closes in October; the 2027 round closed on 20 October 2026.
records.notes: The CSC page confirms the 2027/28 round is open until 16:00 BST on 20 October 2026 and requires an upper second class bachelor’s degree, which is a class of degree rather than a CGPA. Indian candidates must also be nominated by the Ministry of Education through its SAKSHAT portal, which ran a separate nomination window into December for the 2026 round. The Ministry’s own criteria for its nominees could not be read, so this stays unconfirmed until its 2027 notice is checked.

records.title: Türkiye Scholarships Graduate Programme
records.org: Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities
records.summary: A government-funded master’s scholarship for international students at universities in Türkiye, including placement, tuition, stipend, housing and insurance.

benefit.what_you_get: University placement, tuition, accommodation, health insurance and a monthly stipend.

apply.what_you_need: An online application with identity, degree, transcript and programme-choice documents
apply.how_they_select: Applications are assessed for academic record and goals before shortlisted candidates are interviewed

records.typical_window: Graduate applications are accepted each year from 10 January to 20 February.
records.notes: Citizens of all countries may apply except Turkish citizens and people who lost Turkish citizenship. Master’s applicants must be under 30. The minimum academic achievement for graduate candidates is 75% in the degree; the page gives no 10-point CGPA figure, so treat 75% aggregate in your degree as the bar. No Class 10, Class 12, backlog, gap or work-experience cutoff is stated. This degree bar is stated as a percentage or on a 4-point scale, which the app cannot compare with your 10-point CGPA, so the marks rule stays unconfirmed here and you must check it yourself.

records.title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship
records.org: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
records.summary: A scholarship for international students nominated by French institutions for selected master’s and engineering programmes in France.

benefit.what_you_get: A monthly allowance, international airfare, travel support, insurance and housing assistance.

apply.what_you_need: Nomination by the French institution offering the selected master’s or engineering programme
apply.how_they_select: French institutions nominate candidates and a panel of experts selects scholarship recipients

records.typical_window: French institutions run their own nomination windows before the annual Campus France call closes.
records.notes: Students cannot apply directly; a French institution must nominate them and sets its own internal deadline. The Eiffel programme does not pay tuition or fees, despite paying the allowance and listed services. The current candidate eligibility call and institution-specific deadline still need to be checked before applying. Because the nominating institution applies its own academic selection, the rules stay unconfirmed until you read its call.

records.title: IET India Scholarship Award
records.org: Institution of Engineering and Technology India
records.summary: A national award for full-time undergraduate engineering students in India, selected through application review, an online test and presentations.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash awards from a total prize pool, with the top winner receiving the largest award.

location.place: Online rounds and national finals in India

apply.what_you_need: Academic, activity, professional-engagement and outreach details; shortlisted students later provide proof
apply.how_they_select: Application review is followed by an online test, regional presentation and national final

records.typical_window: The 2026 application ran from 13 April to 5 July.
records.notes: Open to full-time first, second, third and fourth-year undergraduate engineering students from AICTE or UGC-approved institutions, in all branches. The eligibility page asks for a minimum 60% aggregate or 6.0 CGPA on a 10-point scale, and for all credit courses cleared in a single attempt, which is stricter than having no active backlog: a cleared backlog still counts against you. IET members get 15% extra weightage. No Class 10, Class 12, gap, citizenship or work-experience cutoff is stated.

records.title: OP Jindal Engineering and Management Scholarship
records.summary: A merit scholarship for top-ranked students at participating engineering and management institutions, selected through a test and interview.

benefit.what_you_get: A yearly cash scholarship for selected engineering students.

location.place: Online test and interview in India

apply.what_you_need: Institution nomination as an eligible year topper, registration form and supporting academic details
apply.how_they_select: Nominated students take an online test and shortlisted students attend an online interview

records.typical_window: The 2026 registration period ended on 15 September, followed by tests and October interviews.
records.notes: Engineering nominees are the first three toppers in first through fourth year for Civil, Electrical, Mechanical and Metallurgical Engineering at participating institutions. No numeric marks, CGPA, backlog, gap, citizenship or work-experience cutoff is published.

records.title: Kotak Kanya Scholarship
records.summary: A scholarship for women entering the first year of selected professional degrees in India, including engineering, based on merit and financial need.

benefit.what_you_get: Annual support for academic expenses until completion of the professional degree.

apply.what_you_need: First-year admission proof, household income below INR 6 lakh and academic and fee documents
apply.how_they_select: Applicants are ranked using academic merit and financial background

records.typical_window: The scholarship is offered to each new first-year batch; the 2026-27 round closed on 30 September.
records.notes: Applicants must be women admitted in 2026-27 to first-year professional graduation at an eligible accredited institution, with annual family income below INR 6 lakh, and at least 75% marks or equivalent CGPA in Class 12. The FAQ permits only a one-year break after HSC. To keep the scholarship you need at least 6 CGPA each year or promotion to the next year. The official page lists no Class 10, backlog, citizenship or work-experience cutoff.

records.title: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
records.summary: Funding and leadership development for students beginning an eligible full-time graduate degree at Stanford University.

benefit.what_you_get: Up to three years of tuition, living and academic support, plus annual travel support.

apply.what_you_need: Separate Knight-Hennessy and Stanford graduate applications, a resume, essays, short answers, transcript and recommendations
apply.how_they_select: Application review is followed by an invitation-only video statement and an in-person immersion weekend

records.typical_window: Runs every year and closes in early October; the 2027 cohort round closed on 6 October 2026.
records.notes: For the 2027 cohort, the first bachelor’s degree must be earned in January 2020 or later, or by September 2027. Military applicants receive a two-year extension. KHS itself has no fee, but the separate Stanford graduate application may charge a fee. The official eligibility page states no marks, GPA, CGPA, aggregate, backlog, arrear or gap cutoff.

records.title: Quad Fellowship
records.summary: A fellowship for eligible-country students pursuing a full-time STEM master’s or PhD at an accredited university in the United States.

benefit.what_you_get: A one-time award for academic expenses plus virtual cross-cultural and professional programming.

location.place: United States, at the selected university

apply.what_you_need: An official transcript, statement of purpose, two short essays, resume, three recommendations and English proof where required
apply.how_they_select: A holistic application review is followed by expert STEM review and a final panel interview

records.typical_window: One cohort is selected each year; the application for the 2025-26 fellows is closed and the page lists the next timeline as To Be Announced.
records.notes: Indian citizens are eligible, along with citizens or legal permanent residents of other named Quad and ASEAN countries. Applicants must have applied to or be enrolled full-time in an eligible US STEM graduate programme. The 2027 application is not open and the page still refers to the closed 2025-26 selection, so the next cycle must be checked.

records.title: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship India
records.org: Amazon Future Engineer and Foundation for Excellence
records.summary: A merit-cum-means scholarship for first-year women in BE, BTech or integrated MTech programmes in India, with technology career support.

benefit.what_you_get: An annual scholarship until graduation, plus a laptop, mentoring and skill-building opportunities.

apply.what_you_need: An online form, academic and income evidence, family verification and a short essay if shortlisted
apply.how_they_select: FFE verifies financial need and academic credentials, then selects recipients on merit and application review

records.typical_window: The 2025-26 round closed on 30 November 2025; the page now refers to notifying selected students by 31 March 2027, so a new round for first-year students is expected in the autumn.
records.notes: Annual family income must be below INR 4 lakh. The official eligibility section says only first-year women in BE, BTech or integrated MTech are eligible, with CS and IT preferred rather than required. The page still prints a 2025 deadline, so the stored batch is the 2025-26 first-year cohort (2029 graduates); the current cycle and cohort year must be confirmed before applying. No numeric marks, GPA, CGPA, aggregate, backlog, arrear or gap cutoff is printed.

records.title: Thiel Fellowship
records.summary: A two-year fellowship for young people who leave university to build a project or company, with an equity-free grant.

benefit.what_you_get: A grant spread over two years, with no equity taken.

apply.what_you_need: An application describing what you are building, with links to your work and online profiles.

records.notes: Applicants must be 22 or younger and must not already hold a university degree. A student may apply, but must leave school to accept the fellowship. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Global Student Entrepreneur Awards
records.summary: A competition for university students who already own and operate a business, with cash prizes at the Global Finals.

benefit.what_you_get: Cash prizes at the Global Finals, with first, second and third place awards.

location.place: Local rounds, global finals in Cape Town

apply.what_you_need: An online application for a local competition and evidence that you own and operate an eligible business.
apply.how_they_select: Judges evaluate the student entrepreneur, business fundamentals, communication and growth potential.

records.typical_window: Deadlines vary by local competition, and the Global Finals are typically held in June.
records.notes: Applicants must be 18 to 30, own or control the business, have operated it for six consecutive months, and have generated US $500 or received US $1000 in investment. Graduate students have an additional continuous-enrolment condition. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: MIT Solve Global Challenges
records.summary: Open innovation challenges for technology-based social impact solutions, with prize funding and a six-month support program.

benefit.what_you_get: Selected Solver teams gain access to prize funding at selection and later opportunities.
benefit.amount_text: Access to a pool of +$1M in prize funding

location.place: Online program, events in New York and Cambridge

apply.what_you_need: A proposal for a people-first, technology-based solution aligned with an open Global Challenge.
apply.how_they_select: MIT Solve selects a diverse portfolio of the strongest technology-based solutions across geography and stage.

records.typical_window: Global Challenges are open for submissions from September to November each year.
records.notes: The open call seeks solutions from anyone, anywhere in the world. Selected teams commit about 25 hours across six months and normally attend events in New York City and Cambridge. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Antler India AI Residency
records.summary: A short, full-time residency in Bangalore for early AI founders, with an expense grant before any investment decision.

benefit.what_you_get: A one-time expense grant during the residency, separate from the potential equity investment.

apply.what_you_need: An AI startup or strong AI startup direction, and availability to join full-time in Bangalore.
apply.how_they_select: Antler curates the residency group and makes fast-track investment decisions within three weeks.

records.typical_window: The 2026 AI Residency closed applications on February 19 for a February 23 start.
records.notes: The page requires founders to join full-time in Bangalore but does not require Indian citizenship or student status. Investment is separate and is not counted as the listed benefit. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Emergent Ventures
records.org: Mercatus Center at George Mason University
records.summary: A rolling grant and fellowship program for people with scalable "zero to one" ideas, with a dedicated track for projects focused on India.

benefit.what_you_get: A grant or fellowship for your own project, with no equity taken; the page prints no grant size.

location.place: Work from anywhere; India-focused projects pick the India track on the form

apply.what_you_need: One application per applicant and project through the online form, with the India region selected if your project focuses on India.

records.notes: Applicants must be at least 13 years old. The program has run since 2018 and takes applications on a rolling basis with no deadline. The page gives no grant figure and says the team cannot advise on individual applications or give feedback. It lists no marks, CGPA, backlog, gap, degree or work-experience cutoff.

records.title: 776 Fellowship
records.summary: A two-year, full-time fellowship for young people building projects that address climate change.

benefit.what_you_get: A grant over two years plus access to the Seven Seven Six founder network.

apply.what_you_need: A climate-focused project, company, idea or initiative that you can pursue full-time for two years.
apply.how_they_select: The program selects 20 fellows and uses a final remote interview.

records.typical_window: Applications are announced by cohort; the page says to check back for the 2026 application.
records.notes: Applicants must be 18 to 24 and can live anywhere. Current students may apply but must leave university for two years if accepted. The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: Echoing Green Fellowship
records.summary: An 18-month, full-time fellowship for original founders building early-stage organizations focused on social impact.

benefit.what_you_get: An 18-month stipend plus leadership development, expert support and a global founder community.

apply.what_you_need: An online application, resume, organization details, short answers and a 60-second founder video.
apply.how_they_select: Expert reviewers score application materials against published leadership and organization criteria.

records.typical_window: The application is open for three weeks; applicants are told to sign up for the next cycle dates.
records.notes: Applicants must be at least 18, proficient in English, an original founder and primary decision maker, and able to work 40 hours a week on the organization. For-profit and hybrid organizations receive a recoverable grant that may require repayment only after stated valuation or revenue and profit thresholds. The official page says there are no educational requirements and lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff.

records.title: HackWithInfy
records.summary: A coding competition for engineering students that can lead to Infosys internships and employment opportunities. Participants compete in coding rounds and selected finalists attend the grand finale.

benefit.what_you_get: Finalists can get Infosys internship and job offers, decided by the coding rounds.

location.place: Online rounds, grand finale in India

apply.what_you_need: Registration through your college placement officer
apply.how_they_select: Online coding rounds, then a grand finale for the shortlisted

records.typical_window: College-led registration usually runs from February into March
records.notes: The 2026 terms and conditions require participants to be 18 or older, resident in India, and BE, BTech, ME, MTech, dual degree, MS (Research), MCA or five-year integrated MSc students graduating in 2027; for the 2027 edition expect the batch to move forward. records.title: TCS All India NQT Hiring
records.summary: TCS uses the NQT selection process to place eligible graduates into Ninja, Digital or Prime interviews based on test performance.

benefit.what_you_get: A TCS Ninja, Digital or Prime job offer, decided by your NQT score and interviews.
benefit.amount_text: Prime tier: 9.09 LPA - 9.30 LPA (the page prints no Ninja or Digital figure)

apply.what_you_need: Registration on the TCS NextStep portal
apply.how_they_select: The National Qualifier Test, then interviews for the Ninja, Digital or Prime tier

records.typical_window: Registration for the 2026 drive opened in mid February and closed on 20 March. The next drive is not announced.
records.notes: The official page requires 60% or equivalent CGPA in class 10, class 12, diploma and graduation. It gives no 10-point CGPA cutoff, so min_cgpa is left empty; treat 60% aggregate in your degree as the bar. Because the app cannot compare that degree percentage with your 10-point CGPA, the record stays unconfirmed and a pass on the school marks alone is not a full pass. The closed 2026 drive was open to the 2024, 2025 and 2026 batches only and capped work experience at two years. The salary figure shown is the Prime offer range for a UG candidate with zero to one year of experience.

records.title: Qualcomm Campus Hiring India
records.summary: Qualcomm hires campus graduates for software engineering roles in India. The role covers embedded software, platforms, connectivity and application development.

benefit.what_you_get: A full-time associate software engineering role at Qualcomm India.

apply.what_you_need: A resume showing your engineering degree and relevant software skills.

records.typical_window: The 2027 campus listing was open in September 2026 and gave no closing date.
records.notes: The official page lists no marks, backlog or gap cutoff. Its education line names Computer Science Engineering, Communication Engineering and ECE, and the minimum qualification also allows a related engineering, information systems or computer science field.
